primary_diagnosis_treated: End-stage renal disease secondary to diabetic nephropathy

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily, titrate up to 5 mg once daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each titration
medications.purpose: Renoprotective therapy for proteinuric CKD and blood pressure control
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I for CKD with ACR ≥ 30 mg/mmol (proteinuric CKD)

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (risk‑equivalent to coronary disease)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 statin recommended for all CKD patients

medications.dose: 500 mg orally twice daily (adjust to maintain serum CO₂ > 22 mmol/L)
medications.duration: Until serum bicarbonate >22 mmol/L, then review every 3‑6 months
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends bicarbonate for CKD stage 4+ with bicarbonate <22 mmol/L

medications.dose: 800 mg orally with each main meal (3 × daily)
medications.duration: Until serum phosphate <1.5 mmol/L, then review every 3‑6 months
medications.nice_justification: NG107/NG203 phosphate binder for hyperphosphataemia in CKD/ESRD

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after calcium/PTH results
medications.purpose: Prevent/ treat vitamin D deficiency and support bone health
medications.nice_justification: NG107/NG203 vitamin D analogue for CKD patients with likely deficiency

medications.dose: Start 2 mg orally once daily, dose adjusted to INR 2.0–3.0
medications.duration: Lifelong — INR monitoring weekly for 2 weeks then monthly
medications.purpose: Stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation with eGFR ≈ 9 mL/min (DOACs contraindicated)
medications.nice_justification: Guideline‑based anticoagulation for AF when renal function precludes DOACs

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually for bleeding risk
medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of ischemic heart disease
medications.nice_justification: NICE secondary‑prevention recommendation for IHD (low‑dose aspirin)

interactions_checked.interaction: ACE‑I may increase INR and risk of bleeding
interactions_checked.action: Check INR 2–3 days after starting ramipril and after any dose change; adjust warfarin dose as needed

interactions_checked.interaction: Statins can potentiate warfarin effect (especially high‑dose simvastatin; atorvastatin lower risk)
Additive anticoagulant effect increases major bleeding risk
interactions_checked.action: Confirm that benefit outweighs risk; monitor for signs of bleeding and INR closely

interactions_checked.interaction: Sevelamer may bind oral drugs, reducing absorption
interactions_checked.action: Take ramipril at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after sevelamer

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention; eGFR 9.5 mL/min
eGFR < 30 mL/min – high risk of lactic acidosis
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury
Risk of hyperkalaemia in advanced CKD
contraindications.alternative: Dietary potassium restriction; monitor serum K⁺

contraindications.reason: May worsen hypercalcaemia; patient’s calcium status unknown

assumptions_warnings: Serum potassium, calcium, phosphate, PTH, and liver function tests not provided – baseline values required before initiating ramipril, sevelamer, and atorvastatin.
Baseline INR not available – must obtain before starting warfarin.
Allergy status unknown – verify no ACE‑I, statin, or sevelamer hypersensitivity.
Bleeding risk (e.g., recent surgery, platelet count) not documented – assess before adding low‑dose aspirin to warfarin.
Exact phosphate level not supplied – sevelamer dose may need adjustment after result.
treatment_summary: The plan initiates renoprotective ACE‑I therapy, statin for cardiovascular risk, bicarbonate for metabolic acidosis, sevelamer and vitamin D for mineral‑bone disorder, and warfarin (with aspirin) for atrial fibrillation and IHD. All choices follow NICE NG107/NG203 recommendations, avoid contraindicated agents, and include monitoring for renal function, electrolytes, INR, and bone‑mineral parameters.
